May 16, 2025 Good morning, Senator Grahowski, Representative Cloutier, and distinguished members of the Committee on Taxation, I am pleased to introduce LD 1899, "An Act to Eliminate Taxation on Health Care
Spending."
I introduced this legislation because I believe our tax code should reflect our
values----particularly when it comes to how we treat Mainers who are doing their best
to take care of their health and the health of their families.
Under current law, Mainers may deduct certain medical and dental expenses on their state income tax only if those expenses exceed a set percentage--currently 7.5%--of their federal adjusted gross income. That threshold excludes many families who are
still facing significant out--of-pocket costs, even if those expenses don't happen to rise above the arbitrary federal limit. LD 1899 eliminates that hurdle. It allows a deduction for any medical or dental expense that qualifies under federal law.
This bill is grounded in a basic principle: healthcare is not a luxury, and it shouldn't be
treated as such in our tax code. When Maine people spend their own hard-earned
money on doctor visits, prescriptions, dental work, or mental health services, they

shouldn't be penalized for it, via taxation on the money they spend on essential
medical care.
This change is especially important for seniors living on fixed incomes, families with
children who need braces or physical therapy, and self-employed Mainers who face
high deductibles and limited coverage options. These are not people looking for
loopholes or special treatment. These are everyday citizens who are doing the right
thing--paying their bills, prioritizing their health, and trying to make ends meet.
LD 1899 is a simple, straightforward way to make our tax code more fair and more compassionate. It does not create a new program or bureaucracy. it relies on existing
federal definitions to determine eligibility and ensures that any qualified out-of-pocket expense--notjust those above a certain percentage--is eligible for a deduction.
This is a targeted adjustment that benefits ordinary Mainers who have the misfortune of needing medical or dental care in a given year. And in a state where healthcare costs continue to rise, we should be looking for every reasonable opportunity to ease that
T
burden--not to add to it.
In closing, LD 1899 is about respecting the dignity of Maine people. It's about recognizing that when someone uses their own income to pay for a necessary medical expense, the government should not come back and take a cut. I respectfully urge this committee to vote "ought to pass" and send a clear message that Maine puts people,
health, and fairness first.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
10055799:
TESTIMONY OF MICHAEL J. ALLEN, ASSOCIATE COMMISSIONER FOR TAX POLICY
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation Hearing Date: May 16, 2025
LD 1899 - "An Act to Eliminate the Taxation on Health Care Spending"
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and members of the Taxation Committee - good morning, my name is Michael Allen, Associate Commissioner for Tax Policy in the Department of Administrative and Financial Services. I am testifying at the request of the Administration Against LD 1899, "An Act to Eliminate the Taxation on Health Care Spending."
For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026, this bill proposes to provide an income tax subtraction modification for medical and dental expenses paid by the taxpayer, the taxpayer's spouse, or dependents during the taxable year to the extent the expenses were not compensated by insurance or deducted when determining federal adjusted gross income.
Eligible medical and dental expenses that qualify for the income subtraction modification must be eligible for federal income tax deductions regardless of the threshold that otherwise limits the federal deduction to amounts paid greater than 7.5% of federal adjusted gross income.
Currently, for federal and Maine income tax purposes, a taxpayer who itemizes deductions may deduct the amount of medical and dental expenses paid during the tax year that exceed 7.5% of federal adjusted gross income pursuant to the Code, Section 213.
1

This proposal will benefit higher-income individuals more than lowerincome individuals due to lower-income individuals having far less Maine income tax liability by which to take advantage of the deduction.
The Administration notes that, as currently written, the bill will allow the taxpayer, the taxpayer's spouse (if filing separately), and the taxpayer's dependent(s) to each claim an income subtraction modification for the same expenditures and for amounts claimed as itemized deductions.
To address these issues, the bill should be amended to: (1) clarify that the income subtraction modification is equal to the amount of expenses paid during the tax year by the taxpayer for the medical and dental care of the taxpayer, the taxpayer's spouse and dependent(s), and (2) limit the deduction to the extent the medical and dental expenses have not otherwise been used to reduce Maine taxable income.
Additionally, the bill should specify that eligible "medical and dental expenses" refer to those qualifying under Section 213 of the Code.
The preliminary estimated fiscal impact is a revenue loss in the range of $200 million.
The preliminary estimated administrative costs are under review. One-time computer programming and related system testing costs are required to add an additional line to the individual income tax return to accommodate the subtraction modification.
The Administration looks forward to working with the Committee on the bill; representatives from MRS will be here for the Work Session to provide additional information and respond in detail to the Committee's questions.
